subject: honey mushrooms
title: The Heaviest Living Thing on Earth Is a Fungus Hiding Under a Forest

scenes.text: The heaviest living thing on Earth isn't a whale or a tree. It's a fungus.
It lives under Oregon's Malheur National Forest: one single honey fungus spread across 2,385 acres.
That's about 1,350 soccer fields. Estimates of its weight run as high as 35,000 tons.
Almost all of it is underground, a web of black, root-like cords creeping a few feet a year from tree to tree.
And it's a killer. It rots the roots of the trees it reaches, and they die over the following decades.
It's at least 2,400 years old, maybe 8,650. All you ever see is a few honey-colored mushrooms each fall.

description:
The heaviest living thing on Earth is a fungus under a forest in Oregon.
A single honey fungus (Armillaria ostoyae) in the Malheur National Forest covers 965 hectares (2,385 acres, about 3.7 square miles), the area of roughly 1,350 soccer fields. Genetic testing showed it is one organism. Guinness World Records lists it as the largest known fungus and the heaviest living organism, at an estimated 7,500 to 35,000 US tons, more than the Pando aspen clone in Utah; it is at least 2,400 years old and possibly 8,650. It spreads underground through black, root-like rhizomorphs at about 0.7 to 3.3 feet a year and causes a root disease that kills conifers over 20 to 50 years, grand fir most often. Above ground it shows itself only as clusters of honey mushrooms at the base of trees in autumn.
Did you expect a mushroom at number one? Comment below.
first_comment: It grows only 0.7 to 3.3 feet a year, which is how scientists know it is thousands of years old. Did you expect a mushroom?
